verifications.claim: YF-VAX is a yellow fever vaccine.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Only one YF vaccine (YF-VAX, Sanofi Pasteur) is licensed for use in the United States
verifications.reasoning: Directly identifies YF-VAX as the yellow fever vaccine licensed in the US.

verifications.claim: The yellow fever vaccine is a single-dose injection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: subcutaneously administer a single 0.5 mL injection; a single dose provides life-long protection; It's given as an injection into your upper arm.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm it is a single subcutaneous injection.

verifications.claim: The yellow fever vaccine provides lifelong immunity against the virus for travelers aged 9 months or older visiting high-risk areas in Africa and South America.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Vaccination normally covers people for life; a single primary dose of YF vaccine provides sustained immunity and lifelong protection against YF disease; YF vaccine is recommended for people aged ≥9 months who are living in or traveling to areas with risk for YF virus transmission in Africa or South America; yellow fever vaccine is recommended for persons aged ≥9 months traveling to or living in areas of South America and Africa with a risk of yellow fever.
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state lifelong protection for ≥9 months old travelers to Africa/South America risk areas.

verifications.claim: The yellow fever vaccine must be administered at least 10 days before travel.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Travellers should aim to get the vaccine at least 10 days before travel; A properly completed ICVP is valid beginning 10 days after the date of primary vaccination; You should be vaccinated at least 10 days before you travel; vaccination at least 10 days before travel.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources specify at least 10 days prior for effectiveness and certificate validity.

verifications.claim: The yellow fever vaccine must be administered at designated, certified centers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: YF vaccination must be given at a designated center; This vaccine is administered only at designated vaccination centers; yellow fever vaccine must be administered at certified yellow fever vaccination centers.
verifications.reasoning: Sources mandate administration at certified/designated centers per regulations.

verifications.claim: Yellow fever vaccine is recommended for travelers to endemic areas in Africa and South America.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Vaccination is recommended to people travelling to countries with a risk of yellow fever; YF vaccine is recommended for people aged ≥9 months who are traveling to or living in areas with risk for YF virus transmission in Africa or South America; yellow fever vaccine is recommended for persons aged ≥9 months traveling to or living in areas of South America and Africa with a risk of yellow fever.
verifications.reasoning: Consistent recommendation across sources for travelers to endemic Africa/South America areas.

verifications.claim: Yellow fever vaccine is required for entry into specific countries.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: several countries ask for proof of vaccination at the boarder; some countries require proof of YF vaccination for entry; Some countries require a certificate showing you have been vaccinated before you're allowed entry; The vaccine is mandatory for all travelers to yellow fever endemic zones as per International Health Regulations.
verifications.reasoning: Sources list countries requiring proof of vaccination for entry.

verifications.claim: A single dose of yellow fever vaccine provides 95% immunity within one week.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The yellow fever vaccine provides immunity within one week in 95% of people vaccinated.
verifications.reasoning: Exact match in WHO source for 95% immunity within one week.

verifications.claim: Immunity from a single dose of yellow fever vaccine generally lasts for life.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Once vaccinated, you will have lifetime cover; a single primary dose of YF vaccine provides sustained immunity and lifelong protection; a single dose provides life-long protection; The yellow fever vaccine provides lifelong protection for most people; a single dose of yellow fever vaccine provides long-lasting protection.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm lifelong immunity from single dose generally.

verifications.claim: A single dose of yellow fever vaccine generally does not need a booster.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: revaccination (i.e., booster dose) is not needed; A booster dose is not needed; All vaccination certificates are now valid for life; boosters are only considered for specific circumstances; a single dose of yellow fever vaccine provides long-lasting protection and is adequate for most travelers.
verifications.reasoning: Sources state no booster generally needed, lifelong validity.

verifications.claim: Side effects of yellow fever vaccine include headaches.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Possible side effects to the yellow fever vaccination include a headache; Reactions to YF vaccine are generally mild; 10–30% of vaccinees report mild systemic symptoms, including headache; up to 1 in every 3 people gets: a headache.
verifications.reasoning: Common mild side effect listed as headache across sources.

verifications.claim: Side effects of yellow fever vaccine include muscle aches.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: mild fever and muscle pain; myalgia; up to 1 in every 3 people gets: muscle pain.
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly listed as muscle pain/myalgia.

verifications.claim: Side effects of yellow fever vaccine include low-grade fevers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: mild fever; low-grade fever; a raised temperature; Reactions to yellow fever vaccine are generally mild and include... low-grade fevers.
verifications.reasoning: Commonly cited as low-grade/mild fever.

verifications.claim: Rare severe reactions to yellow fever vaccine include allergic reactions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Hypersensitivity reactions... Anaphylaxis after YF vaccine; Rarely, a person can get more serious side effects, including an allergic reaction.
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe rare hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis.

verifications.claim: Rare severe reactions to yellow fever vaccine include serious nervous system issues.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Yellow fever vaccine-associated neurologic disease (YEL-AND) represents a collection of clinical syndromes, including acute disseminated encephalomyelitis, Guillain-Barré syndrome, meningoencephalitis.
verifications.reasoning: YEL-AND explicitly covers serious nervous system issues, rare.

verifications.claim: Rare severe reactions to yellow fever vaccine include serious organ issues.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Serious viscerotropic (multiorgan system failure) effects; Yellow fever vaccine-associated viscerotropic disease (YEL-AVD) is a severe illness... vaccine virus proliferates in multiple organs, often leading to multiorgan dysfunction or failure.
verifications.reasoning: YEL-AVD described as rare multiorgan/organ failure.

YF vaccination must be given at a designated center that possesses an official "uniform stamp," which must be used to validate the ICVP; According to International Health Regulations, yellow fever vaccine must be administered at certified yellow fever vaccination centers.
